summary: Describes a format for Message Disposition Notifications and Delivery Status Notifications that carry information about which media features a recipient supports. It lets a sender learn what the receiving system can handle.

eli5.summary: When a message arrives, the receiver can send a receipt that also says what kinds of pictures or pages it can handle, so the sender knows what to send next time.

questions: media features in dsn and mdn
how to report supported media features in email receipts
how do mdn and dsn report media features
subtitle: A way for mail and fax receivers to report which media features they support inside delivery and read receipts.

tldr.problem: Senders in Internet mail and fax need to know what a recipient can handle so they do not send messages that exceed its abilities.
tldr.mechanism: A new Media-Accept-Features field, carrying media feature tags, is added to Delivery Status Notifications and Message Disposition Notifications.
tldr.outcome: Senders can use the information in later messages, but inaccurate data could cause a denial of service.

today: RFC 2530 is a Proposed Standard, and no RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Reporting Media Features
sections.content:
In Internet mail and Internet fax, a recipient needs to indicate the media features it supports so that senders do not exceed its abilities. This memo defines a format for Message Disposition Notifications (MDNs, RFC 2298) and Delivery Status Notifications (DSNs, RFC 1894) that carry this information.

Both have drawbacks. DSNs are not available between all senders and receivers. MDNs require the receiver to disclose disposition information, or, with the denied disposition-type, the time the notification was generated.
sections.eli5: A receipt for a letter can also say what kinds of paper and pictures the receiver can handle.

sections.title: The Media-Accept-Features Field
sections.content:
For a DSN, the field is a per-recipient field. For an MDN, it is an extension field. In ABNF it is media-features = "Media-Accept-Features" ":" media-feature-tags.

The tags are defined in separate schema documents that MUST use the language of the media feature set syntax document and MUST be registered under RFC 2506. A valid example, assuming a schema defines the tags, is Media-Accept-Features: (& (paper-size=a4) (color=binary) ).
sections.eli5: The receipt gets one extra line listing what the receiver can show, like "A4 paper, color".

sections.title: MTA Advice and Security
sections.content:
If the recipient's MTA decides a message cannot be processed, it is strongly encouraged to reject it with status code 5.6.1. This may be returned at the end-of-mail-data indicator if the MTA supports enhanced error codes, or later in a delivery failure DSN.

Inaccurate media feature information could cause a denial of service, since later messages would be sent in forms the recipient cannot process. It may come from a malicious attack, such as a spoofed DSN or MDN, or from misconfiguration.
sections.eli5: If a mail server cannot handle a message it should say so clearly. A fake or wrong receipt could trick senders into sending things the receiver cannot read.
